Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:10:1.hebrew: מאי טעמא דר"מ - דקתני סתמא דמתני', "חייב במתנות":
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:10:1.english: What is the reasoning of Rabbi Meir - For the anonymous [statement of] the Mishnah taught: "[He is] obligated in the [priestly] gifts."

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:10:2.hebrew: אי בכור הוא כוליה דידי - והאי דשקיל אנא הוי חולין, ומהדרנא לך ניהלך, ושקילנא מתנות מיניה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:10:2.english: If it is the firstborn, it is entirely mine - And that [one] which I took is non-sacred, and I will return it to you, and take [the priestly] gifts from it.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:11:1.hebrew: וזבין ליה לישראל במומיה - והדר שקליה לאידך חילופיה. ובכור שמכרו כהן לישראל פטור מן המתנות, דאיתקש לצבי ואיל בפרקא קמא (לעיל בכורות דף יב.):
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:11:1.english: And he sold it to the Israelite in its blemished [state] - And he then took the other [animal] in exchange for it. And a firstborn that a priest sold to an Israelite is exempt from the [priestly] gifts, as it is compared to a gazelle and a deer in the first chapter (above, Bekhorot 12a).

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:11:2.hebrew: עשו שאינו זוכה כזוכה - אע"פ שלא זכה כהן בהאיך, דהא לא מטא לידיה מעולם, עשאוהו כאילו זכה בו. הואיל ומעיקרא הוה שייכא ביה יד כהן, דשמא דידיה נינהו, שויוה רבנן כמאן דמטא לידיה לשום בכורה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:11:2.english: They rendered one who did not acquire like one who acquired - Even though the priest did not acquire that [other animal] — for it never entered his possession — they treated him as though he acquired it. Since from the outset a priest’s claim was connected to it, as perhaps it was his, the Rabbis treated it as though it had entered his possession as a firstborn.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:12:1.hebrew: בספק בכור שאין חליפין ביד כהן - שלא נטל כלום תחתיו, כגון דקתני מתני': "זכר ונקבה — אין כאן לכהן כלום". והאי זכר ספק בכור הוא, שמא יצאה נקבה תחלה, וירעה ויאכל במומו לבעלים:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:12:1.english: In [the case of] an animal of uncertain firstborn status, where there is no replacement in the possession of the priest - That [the priest] did not take anything in its stead, such as that which the Mishnah teaches: “[If it gave birth to] a male and a female, there is nothing here for the priest.” And this male is [an animal of] uncertain firstborn status, lest the female emerged first, and [so] it must graze [until it develops a blemish] and be eaten in its blemish by the owner.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:12:2.hebrew: שחייב במתנות - דהכא ליכא למימר עשאוהו כמי שמכרו כהן לישראל, דהא לא בא בחליפין ליד כהן כלום:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:12:2.english: That it is obligated in [priestly] gifts - For here, one cannot say [that] they treated it as though a priest sold it to an Israelite, as nothing came into the priest’s possession in exchange.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:14:1.hebrew: אי מחייבת ליה - לספק בכור במתנות, אתי למימר: חולין גמור הוא, ואתי למישרי בגיזה ועבודה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:14:1.english: If you obligate him - [with regard to] an uncertain firstborn in the [priestly] gifts, he will come to say: "It is completely non-sacred," and he will come to permit [it] for shearing and labor.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:15:1.english: And can you say [this] - That Rabbi Yosei’s reason is because of shearing and labor:

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:1:1.english: Holds in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili - And our dilemma was with regard to [the opinion of] the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:2:1.hebrew: אי אפשר לצמצם - הילכך לא היו עורפין, דכל אחת אומרת: אני איני קרובה:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:2:1.english: It is impossible to be precise - Therefore, they would not break [the heifer's] neck, for each [town] says, "I am not the closer one."

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:2:2.english: It is possible to coincide precisely - And [he expounds that] "the nearest" [means] even [multiple] nearest [cities].

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:3:1.english: And stipulate - As we explained above.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:4:1.english: That everyone [agrees that] it is possible to coincide precisely - For they hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:5:1.english: What conclusion was reached about it - According to the Rabbis.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:5:2.hebrew: שתי עגלות - דאפשר לצמצם, וקרובה — אפי' קרובות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:5:2.english: Two heifers - For it is possible to be exact, and "near" [includes] even [multiple] near [towns].

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:6:1.hebrew: לייתי תרתי - דהא לא מצי לאתנויי, דהא שתיהן שוות:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:6:1.english: Let them bring two - For they cannot make a stipulation, as both of them are equal.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:6:2.hebrew: א"א לצמצם - הילכך, מצו לאתנויי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:6:2.english: [It is] impossible to coincide precisely - Therefore, they are able to stipulate:

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:7:1.english: The healthy one emerged first - For due to its greater health, it preceded its brother.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:8:1.english: The priest takes the leaner [one] - According to Rabbi Akiva.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:8:2.hebrew: והא משמנים תנן - דמשמע מה שיפה השור מחבירו, ואותן דמים יחלוקו:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:8:2.english: “But didn’t we learn: ‘They assess’?” - Which implies [evaluating] how much more the [one] ox is worth than the other, and they divide that money.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:8:3.english: While you were eating dates in Babylonia - While you were eating dates in Babylonia and pampering yourself.

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:8:4.hebrew: תרגימנא - להאי מילתא דר' עקיבא, ודייקנא לה מסיפא:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:8:4.english: We explained [it] - [We explained] this matter of Rabbi Akiva, and we deduced it from the latter clause:

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:9:1.hebrew: דכי הדדי פליגי - דלתרוייהו יהא חלק בשניהם, ה"נ יחלוקו את החי:
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:9:1.english: That they divide equally - That both of them should have a share in both of them, [so] too, let them divide the living [animal].

Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:9:2.hebrew: שומן יהא ביניהן - מה שאחד שמן יפה מחבירו יהא מוטל ביניהם, ועליו יבאו לדין, ויטעון ישראל לכהן: "אייתי ראיה כו'", כי היכי דסבר ר' עקיבא בסיפא: "המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה":
Rashi on Bekhorot 18a:9:2.english: The fat will be between them - The extent to which one is fatter and better than the other shall be cast between them, and concerning it they shall come to court; and the Israelite will argue to the priest: "Bring proof, etc.," just as Rabbi Akiva holds in the latter clause: "The burden of proof rests upon the claimant."

Tosafot on Bekhorot 18a:11:1.hebrew: עשו את שאינו זוכה כזוכה - הא דאמר בסוף כל הגט (גיטין דף ל.) גבי מלוה מעות את הכהן ואת הלוי להיות מפריש עליהם מחלקם: "הא מני? ר"י, דאמר עשו את שאינו זוכה כזוכה" — ארבי יוסי דהכא קאי; דכולה חד טעמא הוא, דהתם נמי חליפיו ביד כהן, שהרי נתן לו המעות. ולא קאי אדרבי יוסי בפ' שנים אוחזין (ב"מ דף יב.) גבי השוכר את הפועל ילקט בנו אחריו, דמפרש התם טעמא דר' יוסי משום דעשו שאינו זוכה כזוכה — דהתם טעמא אחרינא, משום תקנת עניים, כדמפר' התם: "עניים גופייהו ניחא להו וכו'". והשתא, למאי דפריך, לא קשה מידי בהא דפסיק שמואל כר' יוסי בההיא דשנים אוחזין, ובגיטין לא בעי לאוקמי מתני' דהתם כר' יוסי, אלא אמרי': "לא מוקמינן לה כיחידאה" — שמא דלא סבר לה כר' יוסי בגיטין:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 18a:11:1.english: "[The Sages] rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires" - That which [the Gemara] says at the end of [the chapter entitled] Kol HaGet (Gittin 30a) regarding [the Mishnah]: "One who lends money to a priest or to a Levite so that he may separate [terumah or tithes] on their account from their portion: In accordance with whose [view] is this? It is Rabbi Yosei, who said [that the Sages] rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires" — it refers to [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei here [in Bekhorot]. For it is all one reasoning: for there too, its exchange is in the hand of the priest, as he already gave him the money. And it does not refer to [the statement of] Rabbi Yosei in the chapter [entitled] Shenayim Ochazim (Bava Metzia 12a) regarding "One who hires a laborer, his son may glean after him," where [the Gemara] there explains Rabbi Yosei's reasoning [as being] because [the Sages] rendered one who does not acquire like one who acquires. For there [the reason is] a different reason, on account of an ordinance for the poor, as [the Gemara] explains there: "The poor themselves prefer it, etc." And now, as for that which is asked, there is no difficulty at all: regarding that which Shmuel ruled in accordance with Rabbi Yosei in that [ruling] of Shenayim Ochazim, yet in Gittin he did not want to establish the Mishnah there in accordance with Rabbi Yosei, but rather we say: "We do not establish it in accordance with an individual [opinion]" — [this is because] perhaps he does not hold in accordance with Rabbi Yosei in Gittin.

Tosafot on Bekhorot 18a:8:1.hebrew: אדאכלת כפנייתא בבבל תרגימנא - פירש בקונטרס: בעוד שהייתה אוכל תמרים בבבל ומעדן את עצמך — טרחנו ליישבה. וכן פירש רבינו שמואל בפ' בית כור (ב"ב דף קז:). וקשה: דהוה ליה למנקט תמרים, דכפנייתא הוא לשון גריעותא, כדאמר בריש בכל מערבין (עירובין דף כח:): דכפניות אין ניקחות בכסף מעשר. אלא אומר, דה"פ: מוטב שיהיה לך להיות אצלי ולטרוח בהלכה ולפרשה, משהייתה אוכל כפניות בבבל:
Tosafot on Bekhorot 18a:8:1.english: "While you were eating dates in Babylonia, we explained it" - Rashi explained: While you were eating dates in Babylonia and pampering yourself, we toiled to resolve it. And so explained Rabbeinu Shmuel [Rashbam] in the chapter [entitled] Beit Kor (Bava Batra 107b). And this is difficult, as he should have used [the word] temarim [dates], since kefaniyata is a term denoting inferiority, as [the Gemara] says at the beginning of [the chapter entitled] Bekhol Me’arvin (Eruvin 28b) that kefaniyot [unripe dates] may not be purchased with second-tithe money. Rather, [the author] says that this is its explanation: It would have been better for you to be with me and to toil in the halakhah and explain it, than for you to be eating [inferior] dates in Babylonia.
